findings.issue_text: Webhook secret comparison uses non-constant-time `!==` string comparison against a user-controlled header, enabling timing attacks to brute-force CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET
Webhook endpoint lacks rate limiting, allowing iterative brute-forcing of the secret and writing arbitrary encrypted credentials for any userId/appSlug pair

Salesforce CalendarService refresh-token fetch runs unconditionally on every getConnection()/instantiation instead of only when the token is expired, causing an unnecessary network round-trip and OAuth refresh on every use
Salesforce CalendarService fetches a new access token but doesn't use it when constructing the jsforce.Connection, so the refreshed token is discarded

Salesforce CalendarService checks `response.statusText !== "OK"` to detect HTTP failure, which is unreliable since statusText isn't guaranteed to be exactly 'OK' (e.g., empty in HTTP/2); should use response.ok or response.status

Office365 CalendarService removed console.error logging on zod parse failure while parseRefreshTokenResponse now throws on schema mismatch, and the throw isn't caught, causing a potential unhandled rejection instead of graceful degradation
refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response without checking response.ok when credential sync is enabled, causing callers expecting a `.data` property to silently get undefined tokens
parseRefreshTokenResponse sets refresh_token to the literal string "refresh_token" when missing instead of falling back to the existing refresh token, corrupting the credential
Webhook handler passes req.body to .parse() without verifying req.method is POST or validating body size/content-type, allowing any HTTP method to be processed
.env.example CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY comment claims 32 bytes for AES256 but suggests generating with `openssl rand -base64 24`, which produces only 24 bytes
zoho-bigin CalendarService passes credentialId instead of credential.userId to refreshOAuthTokens, inconsistent with other integrations and potentially breaking the sync-endpoint payload
CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is added out of alphabetical order in turbo.json's env var list, breaking the existing sorting convention

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Office365 CalendarService removed console.error logging on zod parse failure while parseRefreshTokenResponse now throws on schema mismatch, and the throw isn't caught, causing a potential unhandled rejection instead of graceful degradation

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the code changed from `refreshTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(...)` (which never throws) to `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)`. The new helper explicitly does `schema.safeParse(...)` and then `throw new Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` when parsing fails. In `refreshAccessToken`, this call is not wrapped in any `try/catch`, and the prior non-throwing path (plus `console.error` logging on parse failure) was removed. So the diff introduces a real behavioral change: schema mismatches now reject/throw from this async flow instead of continuing with existing credentials, and there is no local handling/logging here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Webhook handler passes req.body to .parse() without verifying req.method is POST or validating body size/content-type, allowing any HTTP method to be processed

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` handler, there is no `req.method` guard (e.g., `if (req.method !== "POST") ...`). As written, any HTTP method will run the same logic and reach `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)`. For non-POST requests (e.g., GET) `req.body` is typically empty/undefined, so `zod.parse` will throw and Next.js will return a 500 unless caught, meaning the route effectively processes/attempts to process any method rather than rejecting non-POST. The diff also shows no explicit content-type/body-size checks in this handler.

adjudication_records.issue_text: .env.example CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY comment claims 32 bytes for AES256 but suggests generating with `openssl rand -base64 24`, which produces only 24 bytes

adjudication.rationale: In .env.example, the comment for CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY states the key "must be 32 bytes for AES256 encryption algorithm" but then suggests generating it with `openssl rand -base64 24`, which generates 24 random bytes (then base64-encodes them). That directly contradicts the stated 32-byte requirement in the same diff hunk.
